title: Tenant weekly activity skyline mart — compact metrics for burst analysis and SLA attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design and implement a compact, tenant-centric weekly activity "skyline" mart that stores compressed time-series summaries and percentile skyline metrics for Console usage. The mart should be optimized for burst detection, SLA attribution, and cost-of-serving rollups while keeping storage and query costs low. Output will be used by Console dashboards, SLO/alerting pipelines, and cost attribution jobs.

Key characteristics we want: dense weekly rollups per tenant + route, median/95/99 latency skylines (t-digest or quantile sketches), unique user cardinality (HLL), token and request counts, peak concurrency snapshots, and an indicator of whether a tenant exceeded SLA thresholds in the week. The mart is intentionally denormalized to support fast OLAP slicing (tenant, region, model, route) and to be compatible with downstream materialized views used in the Console.

Non-goals: not intended to replace detailed raw event lake tables or minute-level tracing; those remain source-of-truth for debugging and forensic analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly mart populated for last 26 weeks with no more than 2.5% deviation from baseline raw aggregates for request counts and tokens.
Percentile latency sketches (95/99) are queryable via SQL functions and agree within expected error bounds (t-digest error < 2% at 95th percentile).
Query templates for: (a) tenant SLA breach list, (b) per-tenant 4-week burst trend, and (c) top-10 routes by cost per tenant — each runs under 3s on our analytics cluster for 90% of tenants.
Backfill process completes without schema changes and completes within allotted cluster window (see implementation plan).
notes_and_decisions: Use t-digest sketches for latency percentiles to balance accuracy and storage; alternative p-summaries were evaluated but t-digest performed better on our long-tailed latency distributions.
Store one row per (tenant_id, week_start, route, model_variant, region) with compact columns: request_count, token_count, tdigest_bytes_base64, hll_bytes_base64, peak_concurrency, sla_flag.
Retention policy: keep 52 weeks in mart; archival snapshots for beyond-1y queries via external parquet exports.
We will denormalize tenant metadata (plan_tier, industry_tag) at write time to avoid joins in common dashboard paths.
Decided to use existing ingestion job infra (eng-51400) to emit weekly rollups; will add a downstream job to convert to sketches and HLLs.
Storage format: Delta Lake (parquet + transaction log) on existing analytics namespace to reuse compaction / vacuum policies.
implementation_plan: Schema design and review (2d) — produce DDL for mart table including comment annotations for each sketch column.
Prototype ingestion job (3d) — Spark job that reads canonical route_event _base_ table, computes weekly groupings, builds t-digest and HLL, writes to mart staging path.
Backfill orchestration (1d) — parameterized Airflow job to backfill last 26 weeks; monitor memory during sketch creation and tune partitioning.
Create materialized views (2d) — build Console-facing views and grant access to Console analytics role; add CI tests for row counts and sign checks.
Performance tuning & SLO queries (2d) — iterate on partitioning (tenant vs week) and compaction settings to meet 3s query targets.
Documentation & runbook (1d) — describe failure modes, rebuild procedures, and how to interpret t-digest/HLL columns in dashboards.
data_schema_changes: Add mart table: analytics.console_tenant_weekly_skyline with columns: tenant_id (string), week_start (date), route (string), model_variant (string), region (string), request_count (bigint), token_count (bigint), tdigest_b64 (string), hll_b64 (string), peak_concurrency (int), sla_breach_flag (boolean as string), plan_tier (string), created_at (timestamp).
New column encodings: tdigest_b64 stores base64-encoded binary t-digest; hll_b64 stores base64 HLL128 bytes. Consumers should use helper UDFs to decode and aggregate sketches.
Add metastore entry and grant analytics_console role SELECT permission.
queries_and_views: -- SLA breach list (example): select tenant_id, week_start, sla_breach_flag, request_count, token_count from analytics.console_tenant_weekly_skyline where week_start = date_sub(current_date(), 7) and sla_breach_flag = true order by request_count desc limit 200;
-- 4-week burst trend example: select week_start, request_count from analytics.console_tenant_weekly_skyline where tenant_id = 't_123' order by week_start desc limit 4;
-- Top routes by cost per tenant: join skyline with pricing.route_cost_lookup on route and compute cost = request_count * cost_per_request + token_count * cost_per_token.
progress_updates: 2025-02-28: Ticket created and triaged by Analytics PM. Initial schema draft attached to PRD.
2025-03-03: Spike completed to test t-digest memory characteristics on 1 week of data — peak driver memory ~3.2GB per executor for heavy tenants; partitioning strategy adjusted.
2025-03-06: Prototype ingestion job created in branch feature/eng-42190; unit tests for sketch roundtrip added.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Heavy tenants can cause memory pressure when building sketches for high-cardinality route sets. Mitigation: add per-tenant throttling and process heavy tenants in a separate, memory-tuned job.
Risk: Consumers misuse base64 columns (tdigest_b64) without UDFs causing incorrect aggregations. Mitigation: ship UDF library and add column-level comments; disallow direct selects in Console views.

Risk: Query performance regresses when many small partitions exist. Mitigation: benchmark both tenant-first and week-first partitioning and set compaction policies to ensure 1-4 files per partition on write.
